title.narrative: UNICEF strengthened adolescent-responsive national systems by advancing policy reform, participation, and skills development. Strategic technical support contributed to the development and revision of four national policies and strategies: the National HIV Sustainability Roadmap Part A (2025 2030), the National Multisectoral Framework on the Prevention and Management of Adolescent Pregnancy (2025 2030), the National Youth Evidence generated through HIV financing analyses informed Cabinet-level policy briefs, increased domestic resource allocation for HIV and health, and shaped the Zimbabwe National HIV and AIDS Strategic Plan (2026 2030) and the Global Fund Cycle 8 application. Adolescent and youth participation in civic engagement and policy dialogue was expanded through UNICEF-supported platforms, reaching 26,747 children and adolescents. Through innovative public private youth partnerships, UNICEF connected 16,487 adolescents and young people to learning-to-earning pathways, equipping them with market-relevant digital, green, and entrepreneurial skills.
